qud-224.front: A pure liquid with all three qualities of its own — taste, colour and smell — is mixed into water. When does it overwhelm the water?
qud-224.back: Once two of the water's <bdi>أَوْصَاف</bdi> have changed — one may change, not two

qud-225.back: It remains usable — unless signs of the najāsah appear in it

qud-227.back: It remains usable — unless signs of the najāsah appear in it

qud-228.back: 10 × 10 arm-lengths (<bdi>ذِرَاع</bdi>) in area, or 36 arm-lengths in circumference

arbh-183.back: The Prophet's ﷺ prophethood — it is one of the proofs of prophethood, which are a whole field of study

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30, revised 2026-10-07
quduri.front: A pure liquid with only two qualities of its own is mixed into water. When does it overwhelm the water?
quduri.back: Once one of the water's <bdi>أَوْصَاف</bdi> has changed

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30, revised 2026-10-07
quduri.front: Water mixed with a pure solid (<bdi>جَامِد</bdi>) stays usable while what remains?
quduri.back: Both parts of its <bdi>طَبْع</bdi> — its thinness (<bdi>رِقَّة</bdi>) and its flowing (<bdi>سَيَلَان</bdi>)

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30, revised 2026-10-07
quduri.front: Why does flowing water (<bdi>جَارٍ</bdi>) stay usable when najāsah falls into it?
quduri.back: It moves on — scoop from it twice and it is never the same water

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30, revised 2026-10-07
quduri.front: For the Aḥnāf, how deep must a large quantity of standing water be?
quduri.back: Deep enough that leaning down to scoop water for wuḍūʾ does not expose the bottom

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30, revised 2026-10-07
quduri.front: At what point does water become <bdi>مُسْتَعْمَل</bdi>?
quduri.back: As soon as it separates from the body

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30, revised 2026-10-07
quduri.front: What water is <bdi>طَهُور</bdi> but disliked to use?
quduri.back: A small quantity that a cat, or a similar animal, has drunk from

quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30, revised 2026-10-07
quduri.front: Why is water a cat has drunk from still <bdi>طَهُور</bdi>, though disliked?
quduri.back: Cats are an exception, because they live among people

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What lesson about resurrection is drawn from the ḥadīth of creation in the womb?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Certainty in it: the One who makes us through so complex a process, a sign of His might, can also bring us back from the dead

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What lesson about doing important things is drawn from the ḥadīth of creation in the womb?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Be careful and deliberate, and take your time — there is no need to rush or be hasty

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Based on the ḥadīth of creation in the womb, when do the majority of scholars hold that life begins?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: 120 days after conception — the basis for understanding the ruling on abortion

arbaeen_ahadith.front: How does Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam's fatwa on abortion define abortion?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Expelling the fetus from the womb, by drugs or by suction

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What principle does Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam's fatwa on abortion put first and foremost?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Islam regards human life as sacred, wherever that life exists

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What status does the Sharīʿah give a human body after death?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: As sacred as it was before death

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Into which two stages does Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam's fatwa on abortion divide its ruling?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Before the soul enters the fetus (the first 120 days), and after

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Per Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam's fatwa on abortion, what is the ruling on abortion after the soul has entered the fetus (after 120 days)?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Totally unlawful and tantamount to murder — the scholars have unanimously condemned it

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Per Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam's fatwa on abortion, when have some scholars given a <bdi>رُخْصَة</bdi> to abort after the soul has entered?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: When the mother's life is in certain and absolute danger

arbaeen_ahadith.front: On what juristic principle does the <bdi>رُخْصَة</bdi> to abort, when the mother's life is in certain danger, rest?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Faced with two evils, choose the lesser — a principle of uṣūl al-fiqh and the qawāʿid

arbaeen_ahadith.front: When the mother's life conflicts with her unborn child's, why is hers saved?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: She is established in life, with duties and responsibilities; the child is still in the womb

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Per Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam's fatwa on abortion, why is abortion unlawful even before the soul enters the fetus?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: The fetus is part of the mother's body — like her own life and organs, a trust from the Creator that she has no right to abort

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Abortion before the soul enters the fetus is not murder. What sin is it?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Violating the rights of one's own organs

arbaeen_ahadith.text: Circumstances that can allow abortion before the soul enters the fetus: {{c1::conception through rape}}; {{c2::danger to the mother's life or health}}; {{c3::repeated pregnancies severely damaging her health}}
arbaeen_ahadith.extra: Not a closed list. From Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam's fatwa on abortion.

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Per Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam's fatwa on abortion, which pregnancy is not a reason for abortion, though rape can be?
What has been recorded in <bdi>اللَّوْح المَحْفُوظ</bdi>, the Preserved Tablet?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Everything that has happened, is happening and will happen — good or bad from our perspective

arbaeen_ahadith.text: Nothing happens without the will and decree of Allah — even {{c1::all human actions, good and bad, and the intentions and thoughts behind them}} are brought into existence by Him

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What is the human share of choice — the choice to do something or not — called?
What follows from human beings having <bdi>كَسْب</bdi> (kasb)?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: They are legally responsible, and deserve reward or punishment

arbaeen_ahadith.text: The position of Ahl al-Sunnah wa-l-Jamāʿah on human choice lies between {{c1::coercion}} and {{c2::absolute free will}} — we can choose between the choices before us

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Why should one not delve too deeply into qadar?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: It is beyond our understanding — it confused even the Companions

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What does science not fully understand that parallels the limits of understanding qadar?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: How thoughts form, turn into intentions, and turn into actions
